title: Playing behind blues singers for Williams
summary: Allen backed many blues singers on Williams's dates, learned the style in New York, and was told to play rough rather than sweet.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: See, one thing I wanted to ask you before I forget, how about the blues singers? You made records with some of the blues singers. I made quite a few of them.

Tooth Smith, Clarence Smith, Sarah Morton. I can't remember one of them. See, Clarence just recorded all those blues singers. So I used to go over there and play behind them. I made records, Jess Trumpet. Did you ever record with Ida Cox? No, I never recorded with Ida Cox. But you heard of her, huh? Yeah. She used to be in New York. But she's supposed to be coming back. That's good. I always see somebody get some money. I can't even think of all those blues singers. I mean, somebody, when you look in there, I told you about the blues singers coming to New York, I ain't loving it. I mean, many records, yeah.
What was the first time you played that style to a company of blues singers? Did you ever play any of that kind of music in St. Louis? In New Orleans or anything?
No, I think it was my first game there. New York.

Did anybody teach it to you? No. Each one have an individual style, you know. You play something that sounds good. And I played them with Clarence, he liked that. So if I play something else, he scored. I used to play some sweet melody with me playing, Clarence. Come on, cuz. They don't want to hear that. Give me some quack, quack, quack, quack. You like that, man. Come on, quack, quack. That ain't like listening to that. That ain't you. Play some quack, quack, quack, quack. I used to get some quack, quack, quack. I used to get some quack, quack, quack. I used to get some quack, quack, quack. Why do you want to make these records now? They got to play what they want. They don't want to hear you play sweet.
